label: Regulatory screen
blurb: How close the site is to resources that trigger federal environmental review, such as listed species, critical habitat, wetlands, floodplains, protected rivers and tribal land.

headlines.label: Provisional regulatory screen score
headlines.note: Mean of this pillar's variable percentiles among the facilities in view, 0–100

charts.title: Percentile by variable
charts.subtitle: Percentiles run from 0 to 100 among the facilities in view, and a higher percentile means a greater potential impact.

charts.title: Distribution across facilities
charts.subtitle: The dot marks this facility's value on the spread of all facilities in view.
charts.label: label

method: The screen marks resources that commonly require consultation or a permit in a federal environmental review. Final and proposed critical habitat are USFWS designations under the Endangered Species Act (section 7); proposed habitat has no legal effect until made final. Wetlands are National Wetlands Inventory freshwater emergent, freshwater forested or shrub, and estuarine and marine wetlands, a guide to waters that may need a Clean Water Act section 404 permit; a jurisdictional determination decides that. Special flood hazard areas are FEMA 1% annual chance A and V zones, the floodplains of Executive Order 11988. Rivers are designated Wild and Scenic Rivers and Nationwide Rivers Inventory segments (American Rivers compilation). Tribal land is Census 2024 American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian legal land bases: federal and state reservations, off-reservation trust land and Hawaiian home lands, where a federal review consults the tribe under NHPA section 106 and Executive Order 13175. It also includes the Oklahoma tribal statistical areas, several of which courts have held to be reservations since McGirt v. Oklahoma (2020). The other Census statistical areas are left out, and tribes also hold interests in ancestral lands well beyond these boundaries. Listed species are USFWS species ranges with endangered, threatened, proposed endangered or proposed threatened status whose range covers the site cell, the list an ESA section 7 consultation starts from; ranges are coarse, often whole counties, so a species in the count need not occur at the site. Each distance runs from the facility point to the centre of the nearest H3 res-8 cell (about 0.7 km²) within the chosen radius that holds the resource, so it is accurate to about half a mile; it is 0 when the site cell holds the resource, and equals the radius when none lies within it. The site count is how many of the six mapped resources lie in the site cell. Historic places and air quality nonattainment areas will be added when they reach the data catalog. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the facilities in view, with direction applied so a higher percentile means a nearer resource; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. This is a screen, not a determination that any review applies, and all of it is provisional.
